releaseNote.summary: One credential rule for SubFlow start and instance trigger tasks: the mapping decides, blank included.

migrations.title: A same-domain SubFlow start carries the caller's credential by default
migrations.description: A SubFlow child started in the same domain now receives the caller's sub, act_sub, position, client_id and role headers wherever the input mapping did not set the key, the same as a cross-domain child. The child runs as the user the resolved header set describes, so CreatedBy = act_sub and CreatedByBehalfOf = sub. Before, a same-domain child saw only the headers the mapping supplied; a child state with interaction.longPoll.roles now pauses for the caller's roles unless the parent blanks what its caller-role provider resolves roles from (role under the default provider; under morph-idm also the identity headers).
migrations.action: To stop a credential reaching the child, set it to a blank value (empty string, whitespace or null) in the input mapping's Headers; an absent key is filled from the caller. See docs/domain/role-grant-authorization.md#caller-credential-on-instance-calls.

migrations.path: SubProcessTask | StartTask | DirectTriggerTask | GetInstanceTask | GetInstancesTask | GetInstanceDataTask
migrations.title: A blank credential in a trigger task's headers is no longer filled from the caller
migrations.description: For the instance trigger tasks, a credential header (sub, act_sub, position, client_id, role) the task's mapping sets to a blank value is a deliberate decision: it does not reach the target and the caller's value is not added, same-domain and cross-domain. Before, a blank value was treated like an absent one and filled from the caller. Only an absent key is filled. HTTP, SOAP, DaprService and DaprHttpEndpoint tasks keep the older fill-when-blank rule.
migrations.action: A task whose mapping sets a credential header to an empty value expecting the caller's identity to be filled in must omit the key instead. See docs/domain/role-grant-authorization.md#caller-credential-on-instance-calls.

migrations.title: Trigger tasks no longer complete sub / act_sub from Activity baggage
migrations.description: The caller's sub and act_sub for an instance call come only from the hop's request headers. Activity baggage is no longer a source, neither in the orchestrator nor on the Execution host that sends a cross-domain task's request, so a child whose parent blanked sub does not pick the first caller's sub back up from the trace. A hop with no caller (timer, automatic transition) adds no credential.
migrations.action: A flow that relied on baggage supplying sub / act_sub on a hop without a caller must set them in the task's mapping. See docs/domain/role-grant-authorization.md#caller-credential-on-instance-calls.

migrations.title: A same-domain instance call runs as its resolved credential, not as the pipeline caller
migrations.description: An in-process SubFlow start and the same-domain SubProcess, Start and DirectTrigger tasks now run as the user their resolved header set describes — the mapping's sub / act_sub where it set them, the caller's where it did not, nobody where it blanked them — instead of the ambient pipeline caller. A started child's row is stamped from that set (CreatedBy = act_sub, CreatedByBehalfOf = sub), so $InstanceStarter, $InstanceBehalfOfStarter and starter-keyed row-security rules on the child follow the mapping. A cross-domain call already behaved this way; a flow whose mapping sets no credential sees no difference.
migrations.action: A flow whose mapping overrides or blanks sub / act_sub on a same-domain call and still expects the child to be attributed to the original caller must stop setting them. See docs/domain/role-grant-authorization.md#caller-credential-on-instance-calls.

migrations.title: SubFlow mapping Headers that cannot be read fail the SubFlow start
migrations.description: A SubFlow input mapping's Headers is read only as a string dictionary, an object dictionary / ExpandoObject, or a JSON object. Any other non-null value — an anonymous object, a script-defined class, a tuple, a string, a list — now fails the SubFlow start with Instance:100023 before any child is started, same-domain and cross-domain. Before, such a value was silently ignored and the child started without the mapping's headers; under the credential rule that would fill in a credential the author meant to withhold.
migrations.action: Return Headers as a Dictionary<string, string?> or an ExpandoObject. See docs/domain/role-grant-authorization.md#caller-credential-on-instance-calls.

migrations.path: SubProcessTask | StartTask | DirectTriggerTask | GetInstanceTask | GetInstancesTask | GetInstanceDataTask
migrations.title: A non-string value in a trigger task's headers no longer discards the header set
migrations.description: For the instance trigger tasks, a header whose JSON value is a number or a boolean is now delivered as its text, and a header whose value is an object or an array is treated as blank: a credential header is withheld, any other header carries no value. Before, one non-string value made the runtime drop the task's whole header set on a same-domain call and on a cross-domain read, so every mapping header was lost and the caller's credential was filled in for all of them.
migrations.action: None required; write header values as strings to keep the result explicit.
